channel.title: Responsible AI & Neurodivergence, Naba Rizvi
channel.description: Daily curated research feed on ethical and responsible AI, with emphasis on neurodivergent people and serious mental illness.

item.title: Evaluating large language models for assessment of psychosis risk
item.description: Eleven open weight models were run over 678 partial PSYCHS interview transcripts from 373 participants, inferring clinical high risk status and rating severity and frequency across 15 symptom domains against researcher ratings. Llama 3.3 70B reached 0.80 accuracy with 0.93 sensitivity but only 0.58 specificity, and generated symptom scores correlated well with human raters on both severity and frequency. Confabulation that would matter clinically appeared in roughly 3 percent of summaries, and the dominant error mode was over pathologising non clinical experience, which is the direction that should worry anyone building screening at scale. Performance gaps across demographic groups were small but varied by site, and smaller models stayed competitive at much lower cost, which is what makes the human in the loop framing the operative part of the claim.

item.title: AI-enabled passive digital phenotyping of experiential negative symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders
item.description: Avolition and asociality rank among the most disabling and treatment resistant features of schizophrenia spectrum disorders, and clinician rated scales reach them only through infrequent interviews and retrospective recall. This review asks whether smartphone and wearable streams covering mobility, activity, sleep, social rhythm and speech acoustics can be converted into valid clinical endpoints, and the honest answer is not yet, since associations are consistent but modest and a single modality correlation is not an endpoint. The bar the authors propose is analytical validity, clinical validity, longitudinal sensitivity, external transportability and patient meaningfulness, which is a far stricter test than the field usually applies to itself. Environmental confounding, device heterogeneity, algorithmic bias, privacy and model opacity are treated as design constraints rather than parked in a limitations section.
